chapters.summary: God creates the heavens, the earth, and everything in them over six days, then rests on the seventh, having made humanity in his own image on the sixth day.
keyPoints: Creation happens through God's spoken word — ‘And God said’ — not through struggle or conflict with other forces.
Humanity alone is made in God's image and given authority to govern the rest of creation.
The seventh day of rest establishes the pattern behind the Sabbath.
chapters.application: Everyone carries God's image, which gives human worth apart from performance — our work and our rest should both be shaped around that.

chapters.summary: A closer look at day six: the forming of the man, the planting of Eden, and the institution of marriage.
keyPoints: God forms the man from dust and breathes life into him — he becomes a living being, not just an animated body.
Eden is entrusted to the man to work and to watch over, not merely to enjoy.
God establishes marriage — one man and one woman becoming one flesh — as the foundation of human society.
chapters.application: Work is a calling entrusted to us, not just a means of survival, and marriage is a covenant worth tending with care.

chapters.summary: The first man and woman are tempted by the serpent and disobey God's command, bringing sin, death, and judgment into the world — but God also promises a future rescue.
keyPoints: The serpent tempts by casting doubt on God's word and misrepresenting his motives.
Sin brings expulsion from the garden, separation from God, and the burdens of hard labor and death.
God promises that the woman's offspring will crush the serpent's head — the Bible's first hint of the gospel.
chapters.application: When we're tempted, the answer is to hold onto God's word; when we fail, the answer is to look to his grace and promised rescue.
